tasks.short: Handle receipts, petty cash, bookkeeping and routine banking transactions.

steps.what: Receive payments, count cash and issue receipts.
Enter receipts and cash movements into the {ERP} or petty cash register.
Compare cash and bank transactions with receipts; investigate differences.
Prepare payment batches and cash deposit details from approved requests.
Check payees, amounts and authority; approve and release electronic payments.
Securely deposit cash or hand over authorised petty cash.
Post confirmations and file supporting receipts in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Configure receipt capture, matching and payment preparation in the {ERP}, with authorised release in the {BANK}. A small integration attaches confirmations and cash movement receipts to the ledger and sends unmatched items to a queue in the {WORKFLOW}. Cash handling and payment approval remain human actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cash evidence, payment requests and bank confirmations sit in separate places. Small transaction volumes often made integration costs unattractive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing matching and approval features can cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the remaining connectors and validation rules.
tasks.still_hard: Physical cash, disputed receipts and changed payee details require care. Bank permissions and separation of duties must remain intact.
tasks.human_edge: Notice suspicious requests, explain discrepancies and take responsibility for physical money.

ambition.what: A daily cash discrepancy review before the next payment run

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time entering transactions and more time resolving cash discrepancies. They can propose corrections and pause suspect requests; payment authority does not increase automatically.

reach.task: Review cash handling arrangements across office locations.
reach.learn: Cash controls, custody arrangements and approval limits.

reach.task: Identify recurring causes of unmatched receipts.
reach.learn: Reconciliation categories and basic process analysis.

evidence.claim: Receipt capture, bank matching and payment approval are established finance-system capabilities.
Physical cash custody and payment authority limit the share that can become unattended.

assumptions: This is a cash-handling office; cash work may be much smaller elsewhere.
The time shares describe a mixed transaction cycle, including finance approval.
The {ERP} supports matching and payment batches.
Duplicate entry disappears only after receipt capture becomes the source record.
Build ranges cover one office and one bank connection.
unknowns: Actual cash volume and payment methods.
Available {ERP} and {BANK} interfaces and licences.
Payment limits, signatory rules and cash custody procedures.
Who may amend payee records.
Applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can receipt capture create ledger entries without a separate register?
Can the bank connection preserve approval limits and duplicate-payment protection?
Which discrepancy categories account for most investigation time?
new_work: Review unmatched transactions and rejected batches.
Maintain matching rules and connector credentials.
Check that confirmations reconcile to released payments.
Test payee-change controls after configuration changes.

tasks.short: Complete, check and dispatch bills, contracts, policies, invoices and occasional payment documents.

steps.what: Retrieve recipient details, approved terms and document instructions.
Complete the appropriate template and attach supporting documents.
Check names, amounts, dates, attachments and template version.
Approve binding terms and sign documents requiring authorisation.
Send routine invoices and bills through the approved electronic channel.
Dispatch signed contracts and approved policy documents.
Print, envelope and post documents requiring paper delivery.
File final copies and update dispatch status.

tasks.design: Fill approved templates from the {ERP}, {CLM} and {DOCS}, then validate fields and attachments before dispatch. Routine bills leave through the {ERP}; binding documents require signatory approval through the {ESIGN} before release. Store delivery evidence automatically and generate print packs for necessary paper delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recipient records, terms and templates have different owners. Clerks bridge those gaps by copying fields and checking each document.
tasks.enabler_now: Template, signature and dispatch features already exist. Small connectors and explicit validation rules can now be built with less effort.
tasks.still_hard: Nonstandard terms, recipient changes and legally required delivery methods need judgement. A generator cannot resolve ambiguous authority.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a routine document creates an unusual commitment and obtain the right approval.

ambition.what: A document delivery status desk for internal requesters

tasks.altitude: The clerk handles incomplete requests, delivery failures and document exceptions instead of assembling every pack. They can return deficient requests and report delivery status; signing authority stays with the authorised role.

reach.learn: Document versions, signature authority and delivery evidence.
Metadata, retention schedules and access permissions.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx fills governed layout templates, supporting the template-generation building block.
Structured records and approved templates can generate routine office documents without a model loop.

assumptions: The steps describe a mixed queue; billing, contract and paper branches are conditional.
Most documents use approved templates and structured source records.
Approval time is counted in s4; s6 consumes that approval without another review.
Paper dispatch uses documents already cleared for release.
Checks are uncommon; any payment instrument requires the banking controls described in the money-handling task.
Build ranges cover a small initial template set.
unknowns: Document volumes and the actual paper share.
Which documents require signatures or proof of delivery.
Template ownership and approval limits.
Whether recipient records have a reliable source.
Available dispatch and signature interfaces.
research_questions: Which document families can use existing template configuration?
Can dispatch retries avoid duplicate invoices and duplicate contract sends?
Which delivery evidence must be retained for each document family?
new_work: Resolve missing data and failed validation.
Handle bounced messages and returned post.
Review document permissions and retention settings.

tasks.short: Prepare business forms, government submissions and expense reports from records and supporting documents.

steps.what: Receive the request and identify the required form and deadline.
Retrieve source records and ask for missing supporting documents.
Read receipts and supporting documents; transcribe required fields.

loop.input: Residual unstructured supporting documents and a fixed field specification.
loop.output: Typed fields with page references and explicit missing values.
loop.check: Validate types, totals, dates and source references; compare identifiers with source records.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved fields go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured imports handle standard inputs, but varied scans and free text need document reading.

steps.what: Check expense eligibility, totals and supporting evidence against policy.
Populate the current form or expense report and assemble attachments.
Approve expense claims or return disputed items for correction.
Verify declarations and authorise government submissions.
Enter approved government forms in the {GOV_PORTAL} and submit.
Archive evidence and update the request status.

tasks.design: Use forms in the {WORKFLOW} and imports from the {HCM}, {ERP} and {EXPENSE} to collect structured inputs. A bounded document-reading loop extracts leftover evidence, while deterministic checks and templates generate reports and forms. Expense approval stays in the {EXPENSE}; approved government forms receive an upload pack for the {GOV_PORTAL}, with submission receipts stored in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supporting evidence arrives in varied formats, and form versions change. Government portals often require manual entry and separate credentials.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can handle residual scans, while existing expense rules handle standard claims. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of form mappings and upload-pack generators.
tasks.still_hard: Policy exceptions and legal declarations require accountable review. Portal access, changing forms and ambiguous evidence remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve incomplete evidence and know when a declaration needs specialist advice.

ambition.what: A guided expense submission service for occasional claimants

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time helping people complete difficult submissions and less time transcribing evidence. They can return incomplete packs and explain validation failures; claim approval and legal certification stay with authorised roles.

reach.learn: Expense policy, claimant support and exception analysis.
Declaration requirements, document provenance and filing deadlines.

evidence.claim: Doxis extracts fields from invoices and receipts.
Rossum's Fugro case reports invoice handling falling from two minutes to 35 seconds.
Invoice extraction evidence supports the reading component; government form preparation needs separate validation.

assumptions: Expense and government-form steps are conditional branches within a mixed queue.
The initial build covers one expense policy and a small set of forms.
The {GOV_PORTAL} lacks a usable submission interface, so submission remains partly manual.
Structured imports bypass document extraction.
GDPR access, minimisation and retention requirements apply to employee evidence.
Access estimates include checking applicable national employee consultation requirements.
unknowns: Actual form families, languages and submission volumes.
Available structured records and portal upload formats.
Expense policy rules and approval limits.
Authorised signatories and portal credential arrangements.
Evidence retention periods and sensitive-data restrictions.
research_questions: Which inputs can be replaced by structured forms or direct imports?
Which extracted fields need mandatory review before filing?
Can current portals accept generated upload files?
What validation failures most often cause returned submissions?
new_work: Review extraction exceptions and unsupported evidence.
Maintain form versions, policy rules and field mappings.
Capture portal receipts and resolve rejected submissions.
Monitor extraction quality by document type.

tasks.short: Review clerical workloads, allocate tasks, explain priorities and coach less experienced clerks.

steps.what: Combine outstanding tasks, deadlines and blocked items from office queues.
Inspect completed work and identify errors or support needs.
Set priorities and allocate tasks using capacity, skills and urgency.
Explain instructions, expected quality and escalation points to clerks.
Coach clerks and resolve workload, confidence or interpersonal problems.
Record agreed actions and send follow-up reminders.

tasks.design: Combine queue data into a shared workload view in the {PROJECT}, with team-level summaries in the {BI}. The senior clerk makes allocations and holds coaching conversations; structured decision fields generate action records and reminders through the {WORKFLOW}. Keep confidential coaching notes separate in the {DOCS} with restricted access.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful queue information is scattered, while much supervision depends on context and trust. A dashboard alone cannot make fair allocations or coach people.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations can gather queue facts cheaply. Existing task and reminder features can remove follow-up administration without modelling employee performance.
tasks.still_hard: Fair allocation, skill development and interpersonal problems remain human work. Queue completeness and appropriate visibility require continued attention.
tasks.human_edge: Understand why someone is struggling, give useful feedback and balance urgency with development.

ambition.what: A daily team workload rebalance before deadlines become urgent

tasks.altitude: The senior clerk gets a clearer queue and spends less time collecting updates. More of the week goes to coaching and early workload decisions; formal employment decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Plan clerical coverage during demand peaks.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, service priorities and escalation authority.

reach.task: Manage dependencies and blocked administrative work.
reach.learn: Dependency mapping, deadline risks and practical coordination.

evidence.claim: Queue integration, shared workload views and reminders can support supervision with deterministic technology.
Coaching and fair workload allocation depend on context that queue statistics do not capture.

assumptions: The senior clerk has delegated authority to allocate routine work.
The main savings are preparation and follow-up; conversations dominate the time shares.
Managers enter concise decision fields rather than recording or transcribing conversations.
The initial dashboard reports queue health rather than ranking individual clerks.
GDPR applies; national rules determine employee consultation requirements.
EU AI Act classification must be assessed if later features introduce AI-based employee evaluation or allocation.
unknowns: Existing queue tools and whether staff keep them current.
Delegated allocation and escalation authority.
Employee consultation arrangements and applicable national rules.
Permitted visibility of individual workload and coaching records.
Whether existing {PROJECT} configuration can replace the proposed integration.
research_questions: What queue information changes an allocation decision?
Can team-level indicators expose bottlenecks without individual speed tracking?
Which follow-up fields are necessary, and which would create needless reporting?
What consultation is required before introducing the proposed workload view?
new_work: Maintain queue mappings and deadline definitions.
Correct missing or stale task status.
Capture concise decisions and review generated action records.
Review dashboard access and confidential note retention.
Check whether reminders help staff or create extra interruptions.

role.altitude: The office clerk becomes a coordinator of document, transaction and workload exceptions. They can return incomplete requests, pause suspicious items and recommend process changes, while payment, legal and employment authority remains explicitly assigned.
reach: Support the administrative services manager with cash controls and clerical capacity planning.
Support the project management specialist with administrative dependencies and deadline risks.
Support the legal secretary with controlled document packs and filing evidence.
role.ambitious_version: Run a shared office request service that gives requesters clear requirements, delivery status and practical help with exceptions. Use recurring failure patterns to propose changes in forms, handoffs and approval routes.
